title: Artisan: Automated Operational Amplifier Design via Domain-specific Large Language Model
problem: Designing operational amplifiers requires significant expertise and iterative optimization. Current manual and optimization-based approaches are time-consuming and lack interpretability.
motivation: Automating opamp design can dramatically reduce design time and improve accessibility to circuit design expertise while maintaining performance quality.
method: Artisan uses a domain-specific LLM with bidirectional representation to align circuit topologies with structural and functional semantics. It employs Tree-of-Thoughts and Chain-of-Thoughts approaches to model the design process as hierarchical question-answer sequences through multi-agent interaction. A high-quality opamp dataset is developed to enhance the LLM's design proficiency.
key_novelty: Domain-specific LLM with bidirectional topology-semantics alignment combined with Tree-of-Thoughts and multi-agent interaction for automated circuit design.
contributions: Bidirectional representation framework for circuit topology and functional semantics alignment
Multi-agent hierarchical design process modeling using Tree-of-Thoughts and Chain-of-Thoughts
High-quality operational amplifier dataset for domain-specific LLM training
50.1X speedup over optimization-based methods with improved interpretability and success rate

metrics.accuracy: success rate and circuit performance metrics (exact values not quantified)
